def test_sum_squares():
    import math

    # Empty list should return 0
    assert sum_squares([]) == 0

    # Integer values
    assert sum_squares([1, 2, 3]) == 14  # 1 + 4 + 9
    assert sum_squares([4]) == 16
    assert sum_squares([0]) == 0

    # Fractional values (ceiling applied)
    assert sum_squares([1.5, 2.5]) == 13  # ceil(1.5)^2 + ceil(2.5)^2 = 4 + 9
    assert sum_squares([1.1, 2.9]) == 13  # 4 + 9
    assert sum_squares([0.1]) == 1  # ceil(0.1)^2 = 1

    # Negative values
    assert sum_squares([-1, -2]) == 5  # 1 + 4
    assert sum_squares([-1.5]) == 1  # ceil(-1.5) = -1, squared = 1
    assert sum_squares([-0.5]) == 0  # ceil(-0.5) = 0

    # Mixed values
    assert sum_squares([1, 2.2, -3.3]) == 1 + 9 + 9  # 19

    # Larger list
    assert sum_squares(list(range(1, 6))) == 55  # 1 + 4 + 9 + 16 + 25

    print("All tests passed!")

def test_sum_squares():

    import math

    assert sum_squares([5]) == 25, "Test case [5] failed"

    # Negative integers (ceil of negative int is itself)
    assert sum_squares([-1, -2, -3]) == 14, "Test case [-1, -2, -3] failed"
    assert sum_squares([-7]) == 49, "Test case [-7] failed"

    # Floats requiring ceiling
    assert sum_squares([1.4, 4.2, 0]) == 29, "Test case [1.4, 4.2, 0] failed"
    assert sum_squares([-2.4, 1, 1]) == 6, "Test case [-2.4, 1, 1] failed"
    assert sum_squares([2.9, 3.1]) == 18, "Test case [2.9, 3.1] failed"

    # Empty list
    assert sum_squares([]) == 0, "Test case [] failed"

    # Verify against direct computation with math.ceil
    test_input = [0.5, 1.5, -2.5, 3]
    expected = sum(math.ceil(i) ** 2 for i in test_input)
    assert sum_squares(test_input) == expected, "Ceiling computation mismatch"
